tasks.short: Walk rounds of laundry and maintenance, decide repair priorities, pass jobs to staff, follow open jobs, handle suppliers and coach staff.

steps.what: Supervisor walks rounds to check laundry, maintenance and valet work
Supervisor decides which repairs go first
Supervisor passes on repair jobs: phones staff or leaves paper notes today; writes each job as a work order with room, work and priority after the change, without calling round
Supervisor checks each work order before sending: room, work needed, priority and the staff member it goes to
Supervisor sends the checked work order to the staff member's phone
Maintenance or laundry staff mark each job done with a photo in the facility system
Supervisor chases the status of open jobs
Supervisor sorts out problems with laundry and dry cleaning suppliers
Supervisor coaches staff on the floor

tasks.design: The supervisor writes repair and service jobs as work orders in the facility system ({OPS_SYSTEM}), checks each and sends it to the staff member's phone in the order the supervisor sets; staff mark them done with a photo, and the supervisor sees open jobs in one list instead of calling round. Rounds, priorities, supplier issues and coaching stay with the supervisor.
tasks.previous_blocker: Jobs were passed on by phone and paper notes, and status was chased by calling.
tasks.enabler_now: Facility systems send work orders to phones and show status in one list.
tasks.still_hard: Staff must close jobs in the app; otherwise the list goes stale.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing that a leaking machine in the laundry will flood the floor by tonight.

reach.learn: Whether digital work orders cut forgotten jobs.

evidence.claim: FacilityApps offers digital work orders, schedules, clock-in and dashboards for cleaning companies.
Job results tied to named staff can check performance, so the works council must consent.

assumptions: Boundary: from rounds to resolved jobs and coaching; capital repairs are outside.
Input contract: work order types set by the facility manager; staff phones provided by the employer; fallback is phone and paper.

Rounds, priorities, suppliers, coaching and the check and send of each work order keep their full time. s3 keeps 60 because writing each job stays and only reaching staff by phone or on foot drops. s4 keeps 30 for reading the open job list and chasing late jobs. Staff's done mark (s4m) is an ordinary save in the facility system.
Job data are not used to rate individual staff.

already_counted.description: Supervisor reviews the open job list.

incremental.description: No new work beyond the steps: writing each job is shown in s3, and staff's done marks in s4m.

approvals.approved_version: The work order with room, work needed and priority exactly as checked by the supervisor in s3c, sent once to the named staff member's phone in the facility system; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many staff do not read their phones during shifts, so the supervisor still phones for half of jobs and chases more; s3 keeps 85 and s4 keeps 60 (5.6); high: staff work from the phone list (11.6).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Inspect the surface, look up the method sheet, choose product and method, check safety data and explain to cleaners.

steps.what: Supervisor inspects the linens, furniture, flooring or surfaces and their condition
Supervisor looks up the maker's care instructions and product sheets
Supervisor selects the most suitable cleaning materials and method
Supervisor reads the safety data sheet for the chosen product
Supervisor explains the method and product to cleaners

tasks.design: A method sheet per surface and fabric type in the facility system ({OPS_SYSTEM}) lists approved products, dilutions and the maker's care rules, with the product's safety data sheet linked, so the supervisor opens one page instead of searching. Inspecting, choosing and explaining stay with the supervisor.
tasks.previous_blocker: Care instructions and product sheets were in folders and on makers' websites.
tasks.enabler_now: Method sheets with linked product and safety data sheets fit in a records app.
tasks.still_hard: Old or unknown materials still need a test patch and judgement.
tasks.human_edge: Recognising that a stain on antique wood needs a specialist, not a product.

reach.learn: Whether cleaners use method sheets on their phones.

evidence.claim: Method sheets with linked product and safety data sheets can be kept in a records app.
Employers must keep safety data sheets available for hazardous cleaning products.

assumptions: Boundary: from the cleaning request to instructed cleaners; buying products is outside.
Input contract: approved products and method sheets set by the operations manager; safety data sheets from suppliers; fallback is folders.
Inspecting, choosing and explaining do not change.
research_questions: Does damage from wrong products fall?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: method sheets cover only the common surfaces, so the supervisor still searches for odd ones; s2 keeps 70 and s4 keeps 75 (9.0); high: sheets cover most surfaces (19.0).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Get room status from housekeepers, inspect cleaned rooms, tell the front desk which rooms are ready and handle early check-ins.

steps.what: Housekeepers mark each room cleaned in the housekeeping app
Supervisor collects room status from housekeepers: by radio and paper sheets today; after the change the supervisor reads the list of rooms to inspect that builds from housekeepers' marks
Supervisor inspects cleaned rooms
Supervisor tells the front desk a room is ready: by phone today; after the change by marking it passed in the app, which sets it ready in the property system
Supervisor handles urgent early check-in requests with the desk

tasks.design: Housekeepers mark each room cleaned in a housekeeping app linked to the hotel's property system ({OPS_SYSTEM}), so the supervisor's list of rooms to inspect builds itself and the supervisor reads it instead of calling round. When the supervisor passes a room on inspection, they mark it passed in the app and its status turns ready at the front desk without a call. Inspecting and handling early check-ins stay with the supervisor.
tasks.previous_blocker: Room status passed by radio and paper sheets, and the desk was told by phone.
tasks.enabler_now: Housekeeping apps update room status in hotel property systems.
tasks.still_hard: Status is only as good as the taps; a room marked ready too early annoys a guest.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing which room to finish first for a guest who arrives tired at noon.

reach.learn: Whether live status cuts guests' waiting time.

evidence.claim: Housekeeping apps update room status in hotel property systems.
Inspection results tied to named cleaners can check performance, so the works council must consent.

assumptions: Boundary: from cleaned rooms to rooms ready at the desk; guest check-in is outside.
Input contract: rooms marked cleaned by housekeepers in the app; departures from the property system; fallback is radio and paper.

Inspecting and early check-ins keep their full time. s1 keeps 10 for reading the list of rooms to inspect; s3 keeps 10 for marking each room passed. Housekeepers' marks (s0) are their own saves in the app.
Room data are not used to rate individual cleaners.
research_questions: Do rooms reach ready status sooner?

incremental.description: No new work beyond the steps: marking rooms passed is shown in s3.

approvals.approved_version: The ready status of the room exactly as passed by the supervisor's inspection in s2, set once in the property system for the front desk; a room found wrong later needs a new inspection.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: housekeepers forget to mark about half of rooms, so the supervisor still radios for them and s1 keeps 50 (30.3); high: housekeepers mark rooms as they finish (40.0).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Compute hours per site, collect availability, decide leave, build the roster, handle swaps and sick calls and publish the roster.

steps.what: Supervisor works out the hours needed per site from rooms and cleaning frequencies
Cleaners enter their availability and leave requests in the planning app
Supervisor collects availability and leave requests by phone and paper today; after the change only from cleaners who do not use the app
Supervisor approves or refuses leave requests
Supervisor plans and prepares employee work schedules in a spreadsheet

loop.input: Hours per site, staff availability, approved leave, contract hours, qualifications and the supervisor's brief with staff wishes in free text.
loop.output: A draft roster for the period with a short reason per shift.
loop.check: Code checks every shift against the cleaning cao, working-time limits, contract hours and site qualifications and rejects drafts that break a hard rule; no shift is allocated on behaviour or performance data; the supervisor adjusts and approves the roster.
loop.stop: Three attempts; then the supervisor starts from last period's roster.
loop.why_not_simpler: Staff wishes such as school runs and second jobs come in free text and are hard to encode; code still enforces every hard rule.

steps.what: Supervisor checks the final roster before publishing: each cleaner's shifts, sites and hours against approved leave, contract hours and the site needs
Supervisor publishes the roster to cleaners: by message and printout today; by one release to cleaners' phones after the change
Supervisor handles shift swaps and sick calls during the week

tasks.design: The planning system ({HCM}) computes hours per site from the client's room data, frequencies and norm minutes, and cleaners enter availability and leave requests in its app. A bounded step drafts the roster from these and the supervisor's brief; code rejects any draft that breaks the cao, working-time limits, contract hours or qualifications, and no shift uses behaviour or performance data. The supervisor adjusts and approves; only then is the roster published to cleaners' phones. Leave decisions, swaps and sick calls stay with the supervisor.
tasks.previous_blocker: Hours, availability and rosters lived in spreadsheets and phone calls.
tasks.enabler_now: Planning tools check collective-agreement rules, and one drafts schedules from a plain-language brief with the planner able to override.
tasks.still_hard: A roster that meets every rule can still be unfair; the supervisor must look at it as people will.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing who can take an extra shift this week without burning out.
tasks.altitude: The supervisor adjusts drafted rosters instead of building them.

reach.learn: Whether drafted rosters hold up across sites.

evidence.claim: Planbition X drafts a schedule from a plain-language brief, explains each shift choice, and the planner can override.
The cleaning cao runs 1 July 2026 to 30 June 2028; roster rule tables must follow it.
An AI scheduler that allocates shifts on behaviour or traits is high-risk under the AI Act.
A roster scheme sets working and rest times and needs works council consent.

assumptions: Boundary: from site hours to the published roster; payroll is outside.

Input contract for s1: room data and cleaning frequencies entered in the planning system by the operations manager when a client contract starts or changes; norm minutes set by the operations manager; availability entered by cleaners; fallback is the spreadsheet.
Leave decisions, swaps and sick calls do not change.

Cleaners' entries of availability and leave are shown as s2a and are outside the supervisor's savings. s2 keeps 15 for cleaners who still phone or hand in paper. s6 keeps 10 for the release itself; the check before it keeps its full time.
The supervisor still checks the computed hours per site against what they know of each site, so s1 keeps 30%.
unknowns: Whether the works council agrees to the drafting step.
research_questions: How much does the supervisor change in drafted rosters?

already_counted.description: Supervisor adjusts and approves the drafted roster.

incremental.description: Supervisor writes the brief for each period.
Operations manager enters room data and frequencies per site when a client contract starts or changes.

approvals.approved_version: The roster for the period with each cleaner's shifts, sites and hours exactly as checked by the supervisor in s6c, published once to cleaners' phones in the planning system; any change needs a new check before it is published.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: half of cleaners keep phoning their availability and the supervisor reworks much of the draft, so s2 keeps 50 and s4 keeps 70 (39.0); high: most cleaners use the app and the draft needs only adjustments (51.0).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The housekeeping supervisor keeps rounds, inspections and people decisions; calls, paper status and spreadsheet rosters shrink.
skills_to_grow: Running work orders in the app
role.ambitious_version: A supervisor who spends the morning on the floor instead of on the phone.

job.title: First-Line Supervisors of Housekeeping and Janitorial Workers
